# S83 concept selection

## Locked story

Walsall Healthcare NHS Trust reports that an AI scribe reduced documentation time to under four minutes per patient. The film follows the work from phone to clinician-approved note, then turns the same sheet over to reveal the evidence boundary: the BBC corrected its waiting-time framing because that evidence had not been published. The lesson is to measure one job and claim only what the measurement shows.

The narration is locked to the existing 158-word script and canonical word timing. This is visual direction only; no new spoken claim is added.

## Three visual worlds

1. **The consultation sheet (chosen).** One warm-paper record moves from an explicitly illustrative phone/waveform symbol to the Trust's exact approval words and measured result. It never imitates Heidi's interface or implies that it is Walsall's deployed screen. At the correction, the same sheet flips once; its reverse separates the measured documentation task from the unpublished waiting-time evidence. The hook is the under-four-minute result, explicitly labelled “ON AVERAGE,” beside the publishing Trust identity; the signature is the one continuous sheet flip into the two-column evidence boundary. It earns selection because one object links the job, measurement and limit of the claim. Text excerpts remain short, exact and attributed. For the P1 benchmark, one dominant idea per scene, source-native evidence and one readable visual turn are design targets only until an independent reviewer compares the hosted frames beside P1.
2. **The hospital corridor.** The opening hook is a real trust identity plate at the end of a long corridor, with the measured result arriving on a room label. The signature is a red correction light that redirects the viewer from the documentation room to a waiting-time door. It would connect the story to an NHS setting, but it loses because a corridor and doors could imply patient-flow or waiting-time effects that the sources do not establish; it also spreads the two claims across competing destinations.
3. **The evidence desk.** The hook is a clean overhead source page with the under-four-minute result. The signature is a stopwatch and pen that assemble a two-column evidence register over a desk. It is the most literal approach and would keep citations close, but it loses because a sequence of source cards and desk props makes the reveal feel assembled rather than caused by the story; it lacks the consultation sheet's clear single-object transformation.

## Chosen signature

The same clinical note is physically turned over at the BBC correction. The front carries the measured task and clinician approval. The reverse is a source-identified correction slip; a ruled line then separates **DOCUMENTATION TIME** from **WAITING-TIME EVIDENCE**. The left record receives the official trust statement; the right remains explicitly unfilled and says only that the evidence had not yet been published, matching the BBC clarification. The signature is one continuous object transformation, not a decorative transition.

## Craft intent

- Portrait 1080×1920, 30 fps; visual word timing ends at 56.432 s; the composition holds the CTA through 56.533333 s to cover the 56.523 s voice receipt. Exact AV binding and ears review remain pending.
- Warm clinical paper, deep NHS blue ink, restrained red correction pencil, real sourced organisation marks. No generated hospital footage, invented patient data, clinical interface, patient identity, or false Heidi screen.
- Bespoke objects: Trust identity plate, blank phone silhouette and abstract waveform, source-text quotation sheets, clinician-review pencil, two-Trust route, paired evidence register, before/after timing sheet and the spoken-CTA follow sheet. No portrait or product screenshot is used, and no native webpage is recreated.
- Every on-screen text item, quotation and source/date credit is at least 42 px in the 1080×1920 design. Its rendered legibility still requires hosted review.
- Exact Trust logo elements are selected by their observed visible `img` source identity, with src/currentSrc/alt and locator recorded. Logo rights and permission for even the public review copy remain NOT ASSESSED; no logo is approved for final video or other publication.
